question.text:
A CPU generates $\mathbf{4 8}-$bit virtual addresses. The page size is $\mathbf{8 ~ K B}$. The processor has a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) which can hold a total of $\mathbf{256}$ page table entries and is $\mathbf{2}-$way set associative.

The minimum size of the TLB tag is:

  1. $27$ bits 
     
  2. $28$ bits 
     
  3. $29$ bits 
     
  4. $30$ bits
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
The following two functions, $\mathrm{G1}$ and $\mathrm{G2}$, that share a variable $\mathrm{Y}$ with an initial value of $10$, execute concurrently.

$$
\begin{array}{lccl}
\mathrm{G} 1() & & & \mathrm{G} 2() \\
\mathrm{Y}=\mathrm{Y}+4 ;(1) & & & \mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{Y}+5 ;(3) \\
\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{Y} / 2 ;(2) & & & \mathrm{Y}=\mathrm{Q}-1 ;(4) \\
\} & & & \}
\end{array}
$$

The number of distinct values that $\mathrm{Y}$ can possibly take after the execution is $\_\_\_\_$.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider the following two threads R1 and R2 that update two shared variables x and y . Assume that initially $\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{5}$ and $\mathbf{y = 1 0}$. Though context switching between threads can happen at any time, each statement of R1 or R2 is executed atomically without interruption.

$$
\begin{array}{lccl}
\mathrm{R} 1 & & & \mathrm{R} 2 \\
\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{y}+1 ; & & & \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x} \times 2 ; \\
\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}+2 ; & & & \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{y}-3 ;
\end{array}
$$


Which one of the following options lists all the possible combinations of values of x and y after both R1 and R2 finish execution?

 

  1. $\{(\mathrm{x}=11, \mathrm{y}=13) ;(\mathrm{x}=19, \mathrm{y}=22) ;(\mathrm{x}=19, \mathrm{y}=21) ;(\mathrm{x}=10, \mathrm{y}=13)\}$ 
     
  2. $\{(\mathrm{x}= 11, \mathrm{y}=13) ;(\mathrm{x}=19, \mathrm{y}=22) ;(\mathrm{x}=10, \mathrm{y}=13) ;(\mathrm{x}=7, \mathrm{y}=9)\}$ 
     
  3. $\{(\mathrm{x}=19, \mathrm{y}= 21) ;(\mathrm{x}=11, \mathrm{y}=13) ;(\mathrm{x}=19, \mathrm{y}=22) ;(\mathrm{x}=10, \mathrm{y}=13) ;(\mathrm{x}=7, \mathrm{y}=9)\}$ 
     
  4. $\{(\mathrm{x}= 12, \mathrm{y}=14) ;(\mathrm{x}=17, \mathrm{y}=13) ;(\mathrm{x}=17, \mathrm{y}=19) ;(\mathrm{x}=12, \mathrm{y}=12)\}$

question.text:
The following two functions, $\mathrm{F1}$ and $\mathrm{F2}$ , that share a variable $\mathrm{X}$ with an initial value of $5$, execute concurrently.

$$
\begin{array}{lccl}
\mathrm{F} 1() & & & \mathrm{F} 2() \\
\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{X}+3 ; & & & \mathrm{E}=3 * \mathrm{X} \\
\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{A}-1 ; & & & \mathrm{X}=\mathrm{E}+2 \\
\} & & & \}
\end{array}
$$

The number of distinct values that $\mathrm{X}$ can possibly take after the execution is $\_\_\_\_$.

question.text:
Let the page fault service time be $\mathbf{8}$ milliseconds $(\mathbf{m s})$ in a computer with average memory access time being $\mathbf{50}$ nanoseconds $(\mathbf{ns})$. If one page fault is generated every $\mathbf{2} \times \mathbf{1 0}^{\mathbf{6}}$ memory accesses, what is the effective access time for memory?

  1. $52 ~\mathrm{ns}$ 
     
  2. $90 ~\mathrm{ns}$ 
     
  3. $54 ~\mathrm{ns}$ 
     
  4. $70 ~\mathrm{ns}$
